details: Bitcoin dropped to a four-month low near $62,000 over the past weekend, with prices now hovering around $64,000-$65,000. This sharp decline triggered approximately $2 billion in crypto liquidations within a 24-hour period. Market sentiment is currently characterized by "extreme fear" as investors contend with weakening demand and broader sell-offs in risk assets, partly influenced by concerns surrounding AI-linked stocks and upcoming IPOs.
title: Bitcoin Plunges Below $65K, $2B Liquidated Amid Market Fear

details: U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have experienced a prolonged period of outflows, extending to seven consecutive trading days. In November alone, these funds have collectively seen approximately $2.1 billion in net outflows, with about $1.9 billion withdrawn since November 5th. This sustained selling pressure from institutional investors is a significant factor contributing to Bitcoin's recent price struggles.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Seven Straight Days of Outflows, $2.1B in November

details: Strategy, Inc., the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, acquired an additional 485 BTC for approximately $33.4 million between November 9 and November 15. This purchase, at an average price of $68,887 per bitcoin, underscores the company's ongoing accumulation strategy despite the recent market downturn that saw Bitcoin's price drop below $65,000.
title: Michael Saylor's Strategy Buys $33.4M Bitcoin During Market Tumble

details: The total supply of stablecoins has contracted by approximately $18 billion since early October, falling to around $287 billion. This represents the fastest contraction in stablecoin supply since the Terra-Luna crash in 2022. This reduction in stablecoin availability indicates a significant drain of liquidity from the broader crypto market, contributing to the current "running on empty" sentiment for Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies.
title: Stablecoin Supply Shrinks by $18B Since October, Affecting Crypto Liquidity

details: Zelle is reportedly exploring the use of the Solana blockchain for its ZelleUSD stablecoin and facilitating international payments. This potential integration could significantly boost Solana's adoption and utility within mainstream financial services. This development comes alongside other advancements in the Solana ecosystem, such as Ledger integrating clear signing for Jupiter Swaps to enhance user security.
title: Zelle Considers Solana for Stablecoin & International Payments

details: Bitcoin mining infrastructure firm Luxor Technology reported an AI-enabled attack on its Commander fleet-management software over the past weekend. The incident briefly redirected hashrate from over a dozen client accounts to another mining pool. Luxor quickly patched the vulnerability, confirmed no data was leaked, and pledged to fully compensate affected clients for the redirected hashrate.
title: Luxor Mining Pool Suffers AI-Enabled Hashrate Attack
